# Assembled command palette

`make linux-command-test` now runs the native assembled application and the existing public command/settings comparison. It prepares native PCM, Codex, input and cleanup executables, then uses a private X11/Openbox session, HOME/XDG state, session/accessibility buses, network/PID namespaces, masked system bus and devices, and software Mesa. Cargo caches are resolved before HOME changes; execution inside the namespace is offline. No Python setup or interpreter is needed. The shared desktop runner also requires its documented Firefox, xclip, xprop, xdotool and ripgrep prerequisites; this check uses ImageMagick `import` for actual window captures and does not launch a browser.

[The independent reference](released-application-commands.json), SHA-256 `bdcd386a38994641dee48267dafc036507822cf0a977e6d753002a79b64d50c7`, comes from untouched v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Every released Python module is checked against that commit before activation, and imported module paths/digests are checked again after shutdown. The temporary observer uses the actual application, actions, capture, GTK widgets, compatible stores and clipboard. It does not replace handlers or inherit the former smoke test's service overrides. Synthetic audio/Codex executables and a loopback speech endpoint provide external inputs without user content or credentials. The collector remains under ignored `tmp/`, outside native checks.

The new workflow records sixteen states and four layouts at GTK 4.22.4/Pango 1.58.2, with animations and cursor blinking disabled. It extends the existing [eight-workflow application comparison](application-evidence.md) to nine workflows and 72 states without changing those earlier reference observations. Document actions use the current edited Markdown, Save preserves raw recognition, stale busy/identity selections cannot dispatch, and dialogs transfer focus as observed in the release. Escape closes an actual dialog or Live popover while the real synthetic recorder remains alive; a cancellation spy cannot satisfy that check. Shutdown acknowledges cleanup, reaps PCM/provider children and removes ephemeral provider workspaces. Exact speech HTTP requests and the absence of any rewrite `turn/start` are checked.

The retired `linux/tests/command_palette_smoke.py` was introduced in `3df0ccf`, renamed in `19c7579`, and updated in `771c867` and `a4cf1a6`. Its only external caller was the Make target. Shared Python smoke helpers remain because other targets still call them. Its fourteen contracts have these owners:

| Previous contract | Retained observation |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl+P from a native editor | `editor-focused`: actual edited `MarkdownTextView`, private key input and focused search |
| Modal Escape does not cancel recording | `recording` → `dialog-escape-recording`, with actual recorder phase/process |
| Popover Escape does not cancel recording | `popover-escape-recording`, with the same live recorder |
| Copy preserves Markdown and edits | `copied`: private clipboard contains the exact edited Markdown |
| Empty document actions disabled | `empty`: all four public document rows disabled |
| Save preserves raw recognition | `saved`: actual SQLite reply changed, raw recognition unchanged |
| Empty search does not dispatch | `empty-search`: Return leaves the empty palette open; Ctrl+P closes it |
| Stale availability is rechecked | `busy-stale`: a selected rewrite becomes disabled and no provider turn starts |
| Hidden document actions disabled | `hidden-document`: History navigation disables document actions |
| Changed conversation cannot redirect an action | `changed-document`: selecting another saved entry leaves clipboard bytes unchanged |
| Settings focus transfer | `settings` and `settings-escape`: palette closes and the released page behavior is preserved |
| Provisional Live actions disabled | Actual assembled `recording` state plus the existing released `application_shell` `recording-live` catalog case with `live_active=true` on Capture; the former Python check had left Settings visible |
| Narrow dialog fits | `narrow-first`, plus added minimum layout |
| Keyboard selection scrolls into view | `narrow-last`: actual Down keys reach the last enabled settings row while keeping it visible |

The component command comparison remains responsible for catalog metadata, Unicode search, deep preference navigation and stale editor identities. The assembled flow does not duplicate every catalog row. Wide, narrow first/last and minimum captures are full X11 surfaces; the recorded AdwDialog allocation spans its owning window, while its visible content is smaller. Requested window sizes are 1060×780, 480×680 and 420×520; client allocations are 1050×770, 470×670 and 410×510.

Visual review found two real native layout differences behind the wide modal. The conversation header added eight pixels between children where the release has zero spacing. Prompt settings retained GTK's automatic `image-button` class after adding their explicit classes, making each button eight pixels wider than the released replacement class list. The independent reference was extended with the actual Continue recording and Structure control bounds. The native comparison failed those bounds before the owning fixes (`tmp/native-command-layout-before.log`); the release's observed values were not adjusted to native output.

Before conversion, actual Make failed at a positively verified Python/uv trap (`tmp/native-command-before.log`). The first native runner exposed a nested `/dev/null` mount failure (`tmp/native-command-after.log`); giving that namespace its own `/dev` repaired the runner (`tmp/native-command-after-fixed.log`). The original differing images and measured button geometry remain under `tmp/native-command-first-evidence/` and `tmp/native-command-layout-*-evidence/`. The final independent reference session is `tmp/native-command-controls-release-evidence/session.qeHFNS/released-commands-ze94py0d/`.

Final actual Make passes both suites with Python/uv blocked (`tmp/native-command-reviewed.log`). Its private evidence is `tmp/application-commands/run.klfVUL/session.U8oeWN/native-application-commands/`: sixteen observed states, four layout records and four full-window captures. All four captures have zero differing pixels against the untouched release (`tmp/native-command-pixel-comparison.log`), at the recorded renderer/scale. The adjacent conversation/scrolling and prompt Save/Cancel/reset/conflict/privacy comparisons also pass (`tmp/native-command-siblings.log`).

The final full gate passes 139 native tests, zero failures and 68 explicitly ignored environment checks across 98 suites, both strict Clippy configurations, formatting, generated consistency, ShellCheck and diff checks. The remaining Python gate passes 571 tests and Ruff/formatting for 159 files, retaining its existing PyGObject deprecation warning and a non-failing loopback request-exception diagnostic. Logs are `tmp/native-command-final-native.log`, `tmp/native-command-final-python.log` and `tmp/native-command-final-gates-evidence/session.zotz07/`. No hosted runner was used.

Final review keeps the original eight-workflow fixture unchanged and shares the real application setup/shutdown instead of adding a second assembly harness. Test/support code adds 487 lines and removes 250, including the 239-line Python helper; the independent 577-line/31,268-byte fixture and documentation are separate. The extra native support observes actual clipboard, recorder and store effects in place of the former mocks and records failure evidence. Production changes are two owning layout corrections; no test-only production API is introduced. The Make dependency on Python is removed, and contributor/architecture references distinguish current native scope from historical timings.

This proves the recorded X11 command workflow and sampled layouts. It does not close complete application, all theme/scale/accessibility, private Wayland/compositor, physical input/microphone, clean distribution, Python removal or performance acceptance. The portal is disabled consistently with the released observer; separate shortcut evidence owns portal behavior. The installed app/widget remain 1.6.0, and every complete-workflow row remains Pending.
